The `validate_token` function, defined in [auth/tokens.py:17-22], is designed to verify the authenticity of a signed access token and extract the user identifier from it. The function takes two parameters: `token` (a string representing the access token) and `secret` (a string used as a secret key for HMAC signing). It returns the user identifier if the token is valid, or raises a `TokenError` if the token is invalid.

The function works by partitioning the token string into three parts using the colon (`:`) as a separator. It then checks if the separator exists and if the provided token matches a newly issued token generated by the `issue_token` function using the same user identifier and secret. If either condition fails, it raises a `TokenError` indicating that the token is invalid. If the token is valid, it returns the user identifier extracted from the token.

The `issue_token` function signs a user identifier with an HMAC digest and returns a token. It uses HMAC with SHA-256 to create a digest of the user ID and secret, then concatenates the user ID and digest with a colon separator. [auth/tokens.py:11-14]

The `hash_password` function [auth/passwords.py:7-9] securely hashes a password for storage by using the PBKDF2 algorithm with SHA-256 and 100,000 iterations, incorporating a provided salt to prevent rainbow table attacks. It takes a password and a salt as inputs, returning a hexadecimal string representing the hashed password. The function does not raise any exceptions and has no side effects. It uses the `hashlib.pbkdf2_hmac` method to perform the hashing.

The `verify_password` function, defined in [auth/passwords.py:12-14], is designed to securely compare a provided password with its expected hash to prevent timing attacks. It takes three inputs: `password` (a string), `salt` (a string), and `expected` (a string). The function returns a boolean indicating whether the password matches the expected hash.

The function uses the `hmac.compare_digest` method to ensure that the comparison is performed in constant time. This is crucial for security, as it prevents attackers from gaining information about the password's length or characters through timing differences. The function calls `hash_password(password, salt)` to generate a hash of the provided password using a salt, and then compares this hash with the `expected` hash using `hmac.compare_digest`.

The purpose of this function is to verify the correctness of a password without exposing it to timing attacks, which could otherwise be used to infer information about the password. The function does not raise any exceptions and has no side effects. It relies on the `hash_password` function to generate the hash of the password, which is assumed to be implemented elsewhere in the code.

TEMPLATE """{{- if .Suffix }}<|fim_prefix|>{{ .Prompt }}<|fim_suffix|>{{ .Suffix }}<|fim_middle|>
{{- else if .Messages }}
{{- if or .System .Tools }}<|im_start|>system
{{- if .System }}
{{ .System }}
{{- end }}
{{- if .Tools }}

# Tools

You may call one or more functions to assist with the user query.

You are provided with function signatures within <tools></tools>:
<tools>
{{- range .Tools }}
{"type": "function", "function": {{ .Function }}}
{{- end }}
</tools>

For each function call, return a json object with function name and arguments within <tool_call></tool_call> with NO other text. Do not include any backticks or ```json.
<tool_call>
{"name": <function-name>, "arguments": <args-json-object>}
</tool_call>
{{- end }}<|im_end|>
{{ end }}
{{- range $i, $_ := .Messages }}
{{- $last := eq (len (slice $.Messages $i)) 1 -}}
{{- if eq .Role "user" }}<|im_start|>user
{{ .Content }}<|im_end|>
{{ else if eq .Role "assistant" }}<|im_start|>assistant
{{ if .Content }}{{ .Content }}
{{- else if .ToolCalls }}<tool_call>
{{ range .ToolCalls }}{"name": "{{ .Function.Name }}", "arguments": {{ .Function.Arguments }}}
{{ end }}</tool_call>
{{- end }}{{ if not $last }}<|im_end|>
{{ end }}
{{- else if eq .Role "tool" }}<|im_start|>user
<tool_response>
{{ .Content }}
</tool_response><|im_end|>
{{ end }}
{{- if and (ne .Role "assistant") $last }}<|im_start|>assistant
{{ end }}
{{- end }}
{{- else }}
{{- if .System }}<|im_start|>system
{{ .System }}<|im_end|>
{{ end }}{{ if .Prompt }}<|im_start|>user
{{ .Prompt }}<|im_end|>
{{ end }}<|im_start|>assistant
{{ end }}{{ .Response }}{{ if .Response }}<|im_end|>{{ end }}"""
